newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland Electricty asks for MMC referral.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland Electricty asks for MMC referral.

text.p: Northern Ireland Electricity Plc said it has requested that the regulator's price review be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission after the watchdog rejected compromise proposals from the company itself.

"The price controls proposed by the regulator would not allow Northern Ireland Electricity sufficient revenue to cover its proper costs plus a reasonable return and accordingly may be expected to operate against the public interest," the firm said.
It added it would not be able to attain a reliable network or provide approriate customer service if McIldoon's plan were implemented.

"We therefore believe that customers and shareholders, employees and thge Nothern Irish community would all suffer adverse consequences as a result of the present proposals," the utility said in a statement.
McIldoon said earlier that his proposals would cut average electricity bills by about 40 stg and would ensure that future charges fell in real terms.
Shares in Northern Ireland Electricity fell 16-1/2 pence to 326-1/2 in pre-market trading.
